Prevention: After harvest, plough and flood the field to kill larvae and pupae
Cut/slash the weeds around the rice field (on the bund) 30 days after planting
Legumes or vegetable) and maintain proper crop spacing
Harvest crops at ground level to remove the larvae in stubble
Monitoring: Larva feeds inside the stem producing deadheart during tillering and whiteheads during flowering stage.
Scout rice field for dead hearts or white heads 3 times/week
Use sweep net to monitor population
Observe natural enemies (e.g. crickets, spiders, dragon flies, parasitic wasps, and bats)
Use light traps, 12 per acre between 7-9 pm
Use direct control if more than 10% deadhearts during tillering or more than 5% whitehead during flowering are observed
Direct Control: Remove infested plant (dead heart or white head) from field and destroy/ burn the stalk
Remove egg masses by hand from plants
Before transplanting, clip the tip of leaf blades to remove any eggs
Collect stem borer larvae from floating leaves by skimming the water with a net
Restrictions: Stem borers are difficult to control with pesticides, as the caterpillar is well protected inside the plant.
Spray in morning between 6-10 am or in afternoon between 3-6 pm
Killing natural enemies could lead to outbreaks of secondary pests
Nereistoxin analogues; IRAC group 14; WHO Class
